title: Home Oxygen Therapy Setup Service Levels by System Class
content:
# Setup Service Levels — Home Oxygen Therapy

For each Home Oxygen Therapy system class the operations side keeps four setup figures: the hours from a complete order to setup, whether setup is guaranteed on the day of hospital discharge when the order arrives by noon, whether setup must be performed by a respiratory therapist, and how many backup cylinders are kept in the home for power outages.

| System class | Hours from a complete order to setup | Same-day setup on hospital discharge (order by noon) | Setup by a respiratory therapist required | Backup cylinders kept in the home (count) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stationary Concentrator Oxygen (E1390) | 24 | yes | no | 2 |
| Concentrator with Portable Cylinders (E1390 + E0431) | 24 | yes | no | 2 |
| Concentrator with Home Fill System (E1390 + K0738) | 48 | no | no | 2 |
| Concentrator with Portable Oxygen Concentrator (E1390 + E1392) | 48 | no | no | 2 |
| Liquid Oxygen System (E0439 + E0434) | 24 | yes | no | 0 |
| High-Flow Concentrator with Portable Cylinders (E1390 + E0431) | 24 | yes | yes | 3 |

## Distinctions between the classes

- The home-fill and portable-concentrator classes carry a 48-hour setup figure and no same-day discharge guarantee; the other four classes carry 24 hours and the same-day guarantee.
- Only High-Flow Concentrator with Portable Cylinders (E1390 + E0431) is set up by a respiratory therapist, and it keeps the most backup cylinders, 3.
- Liquid Oxygen System (E0439 + E0434) keeps 0 backup cylinders in the home.

## Worked reading (hypothetical)

A hypothetical complete order for Concentrator with Home Fill System (E1390 + K0738) received at 10:00 on a Monday falls within its 48-hour figure if setup is made by 10:00 on the Wednesday; the same order for Stationary Concentrator Oxygen (E1390) falls within its 24-hour figure if setup is made by 10:00 on the Tuesday.
